g1.label: 1. They ___ to a recycling plant
g1.why: The bottles do not move themselves: someone takes them, so use the passive “are taken”, with “then” after “are”.

g2.label: 2. where they ___ by colour
g2.why: The bottles are the thing that is sorted, so the passive “are sorted” is needed (stage 3).

g3.label: 3. ___ they have been sorted, the bottles are cleaned
g3.why: “Once” means “as soon as / after”; sorting (stage 3) comes before cleaning (stage 4).

g4.label: 4. ___, the clean glass is crushed
g4.why: Crushing is stage 5, straight after cleaning, so “After that”; “Firstly” would mean the start of the process.

g5.label: 5. the clean glass ___ into small pieces
g5.why: Glass is uncountable and something is done to it: singular passive “is crushed”.

g6.label: 6. these pieces ___ with raw materials
g6.why: The subject is plural (“these pieces”), and they are mixed by someone: “are mixed”.

g7.label: 7. The molten glass ___ in moulds
g7.why: Glass cannot shape itself, so use the passive; “then” goes after “is”.

g8.label: 8. ___, the new bottles are filled and sent to shops
g8.why: Filling and sending to shops is the last stage (8); “Meanwhile” would mean at the same time.

g1.label: 1. Used bottles ___ from bottle banks
g1.why: “Bottles” is plural and someone collects them: plural passive “are collected”.

g2.label: 2. The glass ___ into small pieces
g2.why: “Glass” is uncountable, so it takes the singular “is crushed”.

g3.label: 3. After the bottles ___, they are cleaned
g3.why: Present perfect passive for a finished earlier stage: have + been + past participle, plural for “bottles”.

g4.label: 4. The mixture ___ in a furnace
g4.why: Passive = is + past participle (“heated”); “then” sits between “is” and the participle.

g5.label: 5. The labels ___ before the glass is crushed
g5.why: Labels do not remove themselves: plural passive “are removed”.

g6.label: 6. water vapour ___ and forms clouds
g6.why: A natural process with no human agent uses the active, and “rise” cannot be passive.

g7.label: 7. The new bottles ___ and sent to shops
g7.why: Plural passive “are filled”, matching “sent” (= are sent) later in the sentence.

g8.label: 8. Paper ___ from wood
g8.why: People make paper, so describe it with the passive “is made”.

g1.label: 1. ___, used bottles are collected
g1.why: Collection is where the process starts, so “First”.

g2.label: 2. ___ the glass has been cleaned, it is crushed
g2.why: “Once” + present perfect means “after this has happened”; “Firstly” and “Finally” cannot join two clauses.

g3.label: 3. The pieces are melted. ___, the molten glass is shaped
g3.why: Shaping comes after melting, so “After that”; “Before that” reverses the order.

g4.label: 4. The bottles are sorted. ___, they are cleaned
g4.why: Cleaning follows sorting directly, so “At the next stage”.

g5.label: 5. The bottles are cleaned ___ crushed
g5.why: “Before being + past participle” is the passive -ing form: before (they are) crushed.

g6.label: 6. ___ the glass has melted, it is shaped in moulds
g6.why: “When” links the two stages in time; “Unless” and “Although” do not show order.

g7.label: 7. Review (Describing Trends): climbed ___ 22%
g7.why: 22% is the figure it reached, so use “to” — from the Describing Trends exercise.

g8.label: 8. Review (Bar Charts): most common in A, ___ bicycles first in B
g8.why: “Whereas” contrasts two facts in one sentence — from the Bar Charts and Tables exercise.
